items.question: What is a technology company store?
items.answer: A technology company store is a self-serve online storefront where employees and teams order approved branded swag, apparel, and gifts on demand. Blossom Rocket implements technology company stores through SplashBrands, so SaaS, AI, fintech, and professional services firms can replace ad hoc swag orders with one approved catalog.

items.question: What does Blossom Rocket do, and what does SplashBrands do?
items.answer: Blossom Rocket handles program strategy, brand configuration, approved artwork, store setup, and ongoing support. SplashBrands provides the company store platform, on-demand production, in-house decoration, and fulfillment.

items.question: How long does it take to launch a company store?
items.answer: According to SplashBrands, a company store can typically be set up and launched in about two weeks once logos, colors, and product selections are approved. Blossom Rocket can also build a free, fully branded demo store so your team can try the experience first.

items.question: Are there order minimums or inventory to buy?
items.answer: No. Products are produced on demand after an order is placed, and single-item ordering is supported, so there are no traditional order minimums and no finished inventory to buy, store, or count.

items.question: How quickly do orders ship?
items.answer: According to SplashBrands, orders from its online stores ship in 2 to 5 business days. Timing can vary by product and decoration method.

items.question: Where can orders be shipped?
items.answer: Orders can ship directly to homes and offices, so remote and distributed employees receive merchandise without a central team repacking boxes.

items.question: Can we give different teams or offices different budgets and products?
items.answer: Yes. User groups and access permissions control which products each team, office, or role can order, and ordering permissions and budgets can be set by team.

items.question: Can we set budgets and approve orders before they're produced?
items.answer: Yes. Purchasing approvals, budget management, and cost centers keep swag spending inside agreed limits, and reporting shows what each team orders.

items.question: Can a store include product brands, events, or sub-brands?
items.answer: Yes. Multi-logo configurations let one store carry a company logo alongside product, event, or sub-brand marks, with each approved logo mapped to the products and colors it may appear on.

items.question: What merchandise programs do technology companies run through a company store?
items.answer: Common programs include new-hire onboarding swag, self-serve company stores, conference and trade show giveaways, client and partner gifting, and recruiting and culture merchandise.

items.question: Can we send onboarding kits to remote new hires?
items.answer: Yes. On-Demand Kits combine branded products, personalized print, and packaging, and ship directly to each new hire's address. Onboarding works the same in the office or remote, because nobody has to repack and reship boxes from a central office.
